stories.title: NASA launches Roman Space Telescope despite Trump's earlier effort to kill it
new_facts: Trump personally called into NASA's press conference to congratulate the Roman team on launch success.
New on-record quote: 'We're just about to set foot off into the unknown.'
Telescope uses a donated Hubble-class mirror originally built for a spy satellite; images need half a million 4K TVs to display.
Roman will take a three-month journey to reach its orbit at the second Sun-Earth Lagrange point (L2).
Telescope will also observe black holes and exploding stars; Roman was NASA's first Chief of Astronomy.
Telescope reached orbit just 10 minutes after liftoff.
stories.line: NASA launches the $4.3 billion Roman Space Telescope to study dark matter and dark energy, a mission Trump previously tried to cancel.
